import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 50

Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set of density $\alpha$. Does $10A$ contain a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - O(\log(1/\alpha))$?

Here $kA$ denotes the $k$-fold iterated sumset, i.e., the set of all sums of $k$ elements from $A$
(with repetition allowed). In `Mathlib`, this is denoted `k • A` using pointwise scalar
multiplication on sets.

*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 50](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.6 Problem 50)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Green50

/--
Let $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a set of density $\alpha > 0$. Does $10A$ contain a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - O(\log(1/\alpha))$?

More precisely: does there exist an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for all $n \geq 1$ and all
nonempty $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with density $\alpha > 0$, the sumset $10A$ contains a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - C \log_2(1/\alpha)$?

The sumset $10A$ is defined as $\{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{10} : a_i \in A\}$, using the pointwise
scalar multiplication notation `10 • A` where `•` denotes the iterated addition of a set.

Note: We model $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ as `Fin n → ZMod 2`, which is an $n$-dimensional vector space
over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_50 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset (𝔽₂ n),
    A.Nonempty →
    let α : ℝ := A.dens
    ∃ (W : Submodule (ZMod 2) (𝔽₂ n)) (v : 𝔽₂ n),
      v +ᵥ (W : Set (𝔽₂ n)) ⊆ ↑(10 • A) ∧
      (n : ℝ) - C * Real.logb 2 (1 / α) ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) W := by
  sorry

end Green50

reformulations.difference: The source’s bound n − O(log(1/α)) is expressed using one uniform real constant C > 0 and a base-two logarithm. Lean also includes n = 0, whereas the expanded docstring specifies n ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since log₂(x) = ln(x)/ln(2) and ln(2) > 0, the constants convert by K = C/ln(2), and conversely C = K ln(2). For n = 0, the ambient space is a singleton, every nonempty A is the full space with density 1, and W = ⊤, v = 0 satisfies the conclusion. /workspace/review/equivalence.lean proves the ↔ between the uniform base-two statement for all natural n and the natural-logarithm statement for n ≥ 1, without using the conjecture’s sorry.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf — Ben Green, 100 Open Problems, Problem 50 and its full comments, p. 25; also Problem 49 for status context. PDF dated 30 January 2026.
https://r.jina.ai/https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf — text rendering of the same source.
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2306.08567 — Tomasz Kościuszko, Counting solutions to invariant equations in dense sets, LaTeX source, Theorem 9 and surrounding discussion.
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration against the source and the checklist. Lean confirms that the selected Finset.nsmul instance gives the tenfold sumset, including repetition; its membership characterization by ten summands was proved. Density is |A|/2^n, nonemptiness ensures 0 < α ≤ 1, translation is the intended coset, and every W is finite-dimensional. Boundary tests and proofs in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean cover n = 0, full sets, and singletons. Green’s current comments explicitly distinguish this still-open Polynomial Bogolyubov problem from the solved PFR conjecture; the cited Kościuszko result is only a partial improvement. The reviewed file was not modified.
